glossary.definition: An agent that acts for a signed-in person. The token has sub = the person and act = the agent, so both are in the audit trail.
The RFC 8693 actor claim: who is acting on the subject's behalf. Each delegated hop here gets its own token with its own act and a narrower scope.
Every tool call goes through one point that allows it, denies it, or holds it for a person to approve. Here that is the Privilege demo.
A run that starts with no person in the session. It only runs while armed (an hour), and a write above its remit parks for a human.
Disarms the unattended lane and cancels every run still waiting on a person, so nothing resumes later.

sources.title: RFC 8693: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange
sources.use: The act (actor) claim and delegation semantics

stories.title: Code and architecture review
stories.say: A signed-in engineer asks the agent to review a pull request. It reads, comments, strays into another team's repo, then tries to merge.

stories.title: Restricted evidence stays restricted
stories.say: An engineer asks the agent for security-event logs and audit evidence. Both are restricted to the compliance group.

stories.title: Sprint planning and story writing
stories.say: A business analyst asks for a draft story, then for an update to an existing one.

stories.title: Compliance evidence collection
stories.say: A compliance officer asks for CIP-010 evidence. The collector delegates to one agent per source, each its own identity. Then one agent reaches for something it should never have.

stories.title: Quarterly evidence sweep (unattended)
stories.say: A schedule fires the sweep with nobody signed in. Reads run; the requirement update waits for a human.
